origin.description: Tune the ICU collator used by compare, order, unique, duplicated, and collation search.
origin.usage: stri_opts_collator(locale = NULL, strength = 3L, alternate_shifted = FALSE, french = FALSE, uppercase_first = NA, case_level = FALSE, normalization = FALSE, normalisation = normalization, numeric = FALSE)

arguments.name: locale
arguments.text: One string. NULL or "" selects the default locale.

arguments.name: strength
arguments.text: Integer 1, 2, 3, or 4. 1 is the most permissive collation and 4 is the strictest. The documented default is 3.

arguments.name: alternate_shifted
arguments.text: Logical. FALSE treats non-ignorable primary weights alike. TRUE moves code points at or below the variable top onto the quaternary level.

arguments.name: french
arguments.text: Logical. TRUE compares secondary weights backwards, as in Canadian French.

arguments.name: uppercase_first
arguments.text: Logical or NA. NA follows tertiary weights. TRUE sorts upper case before lower case. FALSE does the opposite.

arguments.name: case_level
arguments.text: Logical. TRUE inserts an extra case level before the third level.

arguments.name: normalization
arguments.text: Logical. TRUE checks the input for FCD and applies incremental NFD when it is not in that form.

arguments.name: normalisation
arguments.text: Alias of normalization. The stored name is normalization. The primary wins when both are supplied.

arguments.name: numeric
arguments.text: Logical. TRUE orders digit runs by numeric value, so "100" follows "2". Negative numbers and non-integers are not ordered that way.

origin.details: The collator is a locale-aware comparison, not a bytewise one. R also binds this function as stri_coll. Only arguments that were passed are stored, in the order locale, strength, alternate_shifted, french, uppercase_first, case_level, numeric, normalization.
origin.value: A named list. Missing settings stay at the defaults the collator uses. NULL drops that name.

translation.description: Collator settings as a dict of the values that were passed.
translation.usage: stri_opts_collator(locale=None, strength=3, alternate_shifted=False, french=False, uppercase_first=NA, case_level=False, normalization=False, normalisation=None, numeric=False)

arguments.name: locale
arguments.text: One string. None or "" selects the default locale. None is not stored.

arguments.name: strength
arguments.text: Integer 1, 2, 3, or 4. Omit it to leave the setting out. The documented default is 3.

arguments.name: alternate_shifted
arguments.text: Logical. False treats non-ignorable primary weights alike. True shifts variable-top code points to the quaternary level.

arguments.name: french
arguments.text: Logical. True compares secondary weights backwards.

arguments.name: uppercase_first
arguments.text: True, False, or NA from stringi._na. NA follows tertiary weights. True sorts upper case first.

arguments.name: case_level
arguments.text: Logical. True adds a case level before the third level.

arguments.name: normalization
arguments.text: Logical. True checks FCD and applies incremental NFD when needed.

arguments.name: normalisation
arguments.text: Alias stored as normalization. Ignored when normalization is also passed, including when that value is None.

arguments.name: numeric
arguments.text: Logical. True sorts digit runs by numeric value.

translation.details: Names are inserted in the R function's order, so numeric comes before normalization. A longer list warns and keeps the first element. An empty list raises replacement has length zero. norm is ambiguous because it matches both spellings of normalization. normalis selects normalisation.
translation.value: A dict of supplied settings. True, False, and None stand for TRUE, FALSE, and NULL. NA is the missing logical from stringi._na.
